findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_state.py:156 discards checks[].app_id, and lines 194–197 select contribution checks solely by name. If main requires validate from App A, a SUCCESS named validate from App B passes even when App A has registered nothing. This can authorize a passed required-checks gate on the unprotected integration branch. GitHub defines app_id as the App that must provide the check: [branch protection API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/branches/branch-protection#update-branch-protection).
findings.summary: Contribution checks can pass without the GitHub App required by main.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_queue.py:538–542 accepts any non-empty digest from content_identity. template/scripts/task_content_identity.py:30–79 computes that digest without checking whether the named active or archived change exists. A read-only probe using the actual checkout and a mocked managed state naming nonexistent-review-probe returned task_identity.task_content successfully. Thus a stale or invalid state can admit a managed candidate without its contract, contrary to design D4's explicit requirement to fail when the change is missing.
findings.summary: Managed admission accepts a digest even when the named OpenSpec change does not exist.
